dispatch.headline: Grandmother Banished To In-Law Shade At Luminary Glades
dispatch.body:
The soil on Kepler-186f is famously red, but the Luminary Glades promised a regal purple bloom for matriarchs. I purchased their top-tier interment package for my grandmother, expecting her bio-ash capsule to sprout a magnificent twelve-metre crown of violet fronds.

I missed the marker. Instead, I dropped her capsule into the low-lumen sector, a damp hollow strictly reserved for second-tier in-laws such as step-uncles and former husbands.

Consequently, grandmother sprouted as a squat, rust-coloured fungus that emits a dull hum whenever anyone steps nearby. My family arrived expecting regal lavender, but they found only a faint rust toadstool. Aunt Priyanka sat on the damp moss and wept into her hands.

"Your step-uncle Sivan was a junior clerk and he got a weeping cedar," she said. "Your grandmother is glowing like a wet sponge."

The staff refused to move her. Bio-ash flora locks its taproot into slate within minutes to prevent theft by wild grazers, so the gardener merely offered us a screen to hide her from the primary mourners.

By evening, the wake split into two hostile camps across the ridge. The blood relatives stood near the high-lumen trees, while my step-brother used grandmother's dim fungal stalk to read a menu.

Grandmother hated bright light. She would have loved the shade, but as a prestigious memorial venue, two out of five stars.

glossary.gloss: A nutrient-sealed container holding refined human remains, engineered to germinate bioluminescent flora upon contact with off-world soil.
The shaded boundary of a memorial garden designated for low-status or peripheral relatives, planted with faint, low-energy vegetation.
